title: SE 30s Velocity Flash Deck — Pilot Snippets (alpha)
summary: A compact slide pack for Sales Engineers to run rapid pilots and answer high-risk questions in the first 48 hours. Emphasis on 30s value statements, one-click proofs, safe fallbacks, and measurable pilot success criteria.
slides: Cover: SE 30s Velocity Flash Deck (alpha) — purpose: win pilots fast. Who this is for: SEs, Platform Sellers, Integration Architects. Quick ask: get a 2-hour pilot window + data sample.

Why pilots win: 3 core hypotheses
- Customers buy certainty (latency + cost) not model novelty.
- A 48h micro-pilot reduces procurement friction by surfacing SLO tradeoffs.
- Tiny demos that show predictable performance convert faster than long whiteboarding cycles.

The 30s pitch (read verbatim)
'We help you serve LLM features at predictable latency and cost across cloud, dedicated, and private installs. In a 2-hour pilot we’ll prove 95th P99 latency at your sample traffic and show unit-cost estimates; if it fails you keep the learnings and rollback safely.'

Pilot skeleton (2-hour box)
1) Kickoff (15m): confirm scope, success metric (latency or throughput), dataset sample path.
2) Quick deploy (30-60m): bring a compatible model variant, enable prefix caching.
3) Exercise (30m): run representative traffic at 50–200 RPS or batch as customer expects.
4) Readout (15m): show latency distribution, token cost estimate, failure modes, and next-step ask.

Engineer handoff script (30s to ops)
Key facts to give SRE/Platform: pinned model (name + hash), target qps and concurrency, sequence length distribution, preferred fallback model, expected KV cache warm-up size.
Example: model: "llama-3-13b-q4f", qps target: 75, p99 target: 250ms, fallback: "llama-3-7b-int8"

Demo runbook: one-click checks and curl snippets
- Health: curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health | jq .
- Quick generation (50 tokens): curl -X POST ... -d '{"model":"redwood/13b-std","prompt":"Summarize: <sample>"}'
- Measure p50/p95/p99: run loader for 5m using siege/vegeta and capture token counts. (script link in repo)

Pilot acceptance criteria (pick one primary)
- Latency first: 95th < X ms on customer's 90th percentile seq length.
- Cost first: unit token cost < $Y under expected batching.
- Reliability first: <0.1% 5xxs over 1k requests.
Always capture a baseline run and the optimized run and report regression risk.

Objection cheats (30s rebuttals)
- 'We need on-prem only' -> 'We can run a Private control plane and provide audit logs; sample deploy can be on a VPN-hosted staging node.'
- 'Latency spikes concern me' -> 'We’ll pin a model variant and exercise with warm KV cache; we also demo graceful fallback to a lower-latency model.'
- 'Cost is unpredictable' -> 'We’ll show per-token breakdown and two autoscale policies: conservative and aggressive.'

Fallback playbook (what to configure during pilot)
1) Route slow requests to dedicated low-latency pool.
2) Enable model variant fallthrough: high-cost -> mid-cost -> low-cost.
3) Expose circuit-breaker thresholds to customer test harness.
Checklist included in repo.

Success metrics we share with buyer (single slide)
- SLOs: p50/p95/p99 latency, success ratio, mean tokens per request.
- Economics: tokens/sec, $/1M tokens extrapolation, cache hit ratio.
- Ops: restart MTTR, tail error rate, fallback invocation rate.

Email templates & one-liners (copy-paste)
- Kickoff invite subject: '2hr pilot: validate latency & cost for <feature>'
- Customer kickoff body snippet: 'Goal: verify p95 < 300ms on your sample traffic and produce a cost estimate. We’ll deploy a model pinned to your workload and run a short load to show numbers.'

Live demo tips and failure rehearsal
- Show the 'happy path' first (single request latency + tokens).
- Then run a short stress load and show fallback gracefully.
- Pre-record a 90s video of an end-to-end run as a backup in case live infra flaps.

Deal ask & next steps (closing frame)
- Immediate ask: 2 hours of access to a staging endpoint + sample payloads.
- If pilot passes: propose reserved capacity quote template and 30/60/90 production rollout.
- If pilot fails: collect runbook, root cause, and propose mitigations (quantize, routing, caching).
